newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PDVSA restructuring will not cost jobs - Giusti.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA restructuring will not cost jobs - Giusti.

text.p: Luis Giusti, president of Venezuela's state-owned oil giant Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA), told union leaders that a planned corporate restructuring would not cost any jobs, contrary to union fears that up to 12,000 jobs were under threat.
Carlos Ortega, president of oil workers union Fedepetrol, received the news cautiously and refused to rule out the possibility of a strike.
Rather than cost-cutting, Giusti said the main thrust behind the changes was to add value to the business and create tens of thousands of new jobs over the next five years.

"I can say categorically that this does not represent any reduction in personnel at all, not at all," he told union leaders at a meeting in the Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV) on Tuesday. "PDVSA alone is going to need 35,000 new workers over the next four or five years, and 10,000 workers next year."
He said a surge in private investment in Venezuela's oil sector would bring the total figure to about 60,000 new jobs.

PDVSA is planning to dissolve its three vertically-integrated subsidiaries Maraven, Lagoven and Corpoven to create three new horizontal business units. Giusti said the move would bring $12 billion added value in net present terms over ten years, after the $300 million costs.

Fedepetrol's Ortega said unions had not been consulted over the changes and feared an erosion of workers' rights to collective bargaining and job security. After the meeting, he set up a committee with PDVSA to ensure that workers' rights would not be affected by the changes.
Ortega did not specify when the strike might be called for or how long it would last, but Giusti said conflict was not the way forward.

"I accept... that we probably failed to do some things in achieving this restructuring, but I do not accept that it is our intention to denationalise or sack people or violate job security or dishonor collective agreements," Giusti said.
During the meeting, regional union representatives said they had already seen people sacked due to the restructuring, but Guisti said this was not possible as the process had not started.
Giusti said the $12 billion would be generated by optimising working capital, maximising use of resources and improving coordination among units.
